measured_on: Intel Core Ultra 9 285H, x86-64, single P-core, dudect at 1e5 measurements/batch
headline: dudect detects the synthetic secret-dependent branch (max-t ~7900) and stays clean on both constant-time controls, so the harness discriminates. It MISSES KyberSlash on this x86-64 CPU: the vulnerable -Os build contains a real idiv (confirmed by disassembly), but a 16-bit division's latency variation on this divider is below dudect's detection threshold at 1e5 measurements. The published KyberSlash attack needs the Arm Cortex-A7's slower, more data-dependent divider. This is a real recall gap for a widely-installed tool on common hardware, and it is exactly the kind of finding the corpus exists to make measurable.
recall_status: No recall figure over the deployed recall-eligible pairs is reportable yet: dudect is a timing tool and both recall-eligible pairs (Minerva, TPM-FAIL) are scored on recorded observations with no runnable harness, so dudect is inapplicable to them by construction. KyberSlash has a runnable harness but is tier C. An honest recall number awaits either Arm acquisition (making KyberSlash tier A) or a statistical adapter applicable to the observation-based pairs.
